gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be at work — I've just seen him at the beach.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses something the evidence rules out.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have missed the train, or perhaps the car broke down — there is no way of knowing.
gaps.explanation: 'Might have missed' — possible but not certain.

gaps.sentence: ___ I get you something from the shop while I am out?
gaps.hint: making an offer with shall I
gaps.explanation: 'Shall I' offers to do something: Shall.

gaps.sentence: He ___ spend so much time on his phone; it is affecting his sleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't' advises against an action: shouldn't spend.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: You ___ tell anyone about this — it is a secret.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' makes it clear the action is not allowed: mustn't tell.
